newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: London coffee seen diving, Vietnam in sell mode.
newsitem.headline: London coffee seen diving, Vietnam in sell mode.

text.p: London robusta coffee futures prices are seen diving at the opening by up to US$100, which may prompt origin sellers in Vietnam to step up sales before the price plummets further, regional traders said on Wednesday.
"I think London will come in about $100 lower at the opening," the chief dealer of a European coffee trading house told Reuters.
"The rally has been shorted out. It's due $100 down this afternoon, " a dealer in a European commodity company said.
Far East traders said the benchmark May LIFFE contract, which slid below $1,600 a tonne to end on Tuesday at $1,560, may eventually find strong support at $1,500 a tonne.
"It really depends on what the funds and specs (speculators) are going to do this afternoon," a trader said.
London will also be looking for leads after the release of what the market sees as neutral U.S. GCA green coffee stocks data released after New York's close on Tuesday, dealers said.
Supplies of green coffee stored in U.S. warehouses rose in January by 15,000 60-kg bags to 1,264 million bags, the Green Coffee Association of New York said.
Regional traders said London robusta coffee futures may move back into a range between $1,450-$1,650 a tonne.
Vietnamese robusta coffee prices were hammered by the sharp fall in London and on the U.S. CSCE arabica contract.

The price of Vietnam's benchmark Grade 2, 8.0 percent black and broken, was quoted by regional traders at around $1,240 to $1,300 a tonne FOB Saigon after being quoted at $1,390-$1,400 a tonne last Friday.

"My guess is some Vietnamese will be in a bit of a panic," one trader with a Singapore-based commodity house said. "They'll probably try to ship out as much coffee as they can before the price drops further."
"If the market stays this way, the price of Vietnamese coffee may come down to $1,200 a tonne," a trader said.
Another coffee dealer said Vietnamese robusta coffee prices are due to come down by up to $300 from the peak last week of about $1,400 a tonne.
"We're already trying to buy at $1,100 a tonne," he said.
Congestion in the port of Ho Chi Minh city may also make it difficult to accelerate the shipment of coffee out of the country, traders said.
"It's still a bit congested, especially since we're just coming out of Chinese New Year," a dealer said, adding most people did not report back to work until this week.
The Tet Lunar New Year was celebrated on February 7 and 8.
But one coffee analyst said the impact of the price gyrations in London and New York will not affect Vietnam as a whole.
"They've been aggressive sellers regardless of where the market is. I believe two-thirds of the Vietnamese coffee crop has already been either sold or committed," the analyst said.
Vietnam's 1996/97 (November/January) robusta coffee crop is expected to have reached about 250,000 to 270,000 tonnes.
In Indonesia, traders said preliminary estimates of robusta beans available for export this season could reach around 320,000 tonnes.
"I think there's some new crop already trickling in, but most of it is still old crop," a dealer with a European commodity company said.
Indonesia's benchmark Grade 4 coffee was being quoted by dealers at around $1,400-$1,500 a tonne FOB Panjang.
Some 4,000 tonnes were traded on the Singapore Commodity Exchange (SICOM) on Tuesday against a total of 4,500 tonnes on Monday.

A total of 1,500 tonnes of the May contract was settled at $1,473 a tonne, 1,000 tonnes of the July contract settled at $1,468 a tonne and 1,500 tonnes of the September contract was concluded at $1,461 a tonne.
-- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
